fields.effect_measure: principal components and factor analysis (5 factors, 73.7% variance), stepwise OLS regressions of water-supply and sanitation coverage, k-means clustering into 5 country profiles
fields.effect_estimate: Stepwise OLS (standardised betas): water supply coverage (adj R2 0.686) -- GDP per capita 0.305 (p = 0.005), % irrigation 0.196 (p = 0.003), urban population 0.179 (p = 0.038), % slums -0.333 (p = 0.001); sanitation coverage (adj R2 0.635) -- total water withdrawal 0.287 (p < 0.0001), urban population 0.259 (p = 0.002), % slums -0.432 (p < 0.0001). Governance indicators (World Bank WGI: voice and accountability, political stability, government effectiveness) load on factors (ODA, country environmental concern) but are not among the selected key predictors of coverage. Informal urbanisation is the strongest negative factor. Five country profiles identified.
fields.covariates: 25 variables from the WatSan4Dev database (income, urbanisation, slums, irrigation, withdrawals, health, ODA, WGI governance indicators)
fields.model_type: PCA/factor analysis, stepwise OLS, k-means clustering
fields.study_design: cross-national ecological cross-section of 101 developing countries (database description and exploratory analysis)
fields.section: Full text (Hydrol. Earth Syst. Sci. 16:3791-3816): 3 Methods; 4 Results (4.1-4.3, Tables 4-6); 5 Discussion; 6 Conclusions
fields.exact_location: Methods p3794-3797; Table 4 factor matrix p3801; Tables 5-6 regressions p3802-3803; country profiles 4.3 p3803-3806

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a cross-national exploratory analysis of 101 developing countries (WatSan4Dev database) read in full text 2026-10-04. Informal urbanisation (slums) is the strongest negative predictor of water-supply and sanitation coverage; income, irrigation and urbanisation are positive; governance indicators are not retained as key predictors. Ecological, non-causal.
